cold.queue_visible.ms.small.how: spawn to first frame on a warm store: the queue is the first pane (median of 3 probe(s)). Re-blessed by `reco-axp` at the median of ten probes of one tree on the reference box — times divided by that runner's calibration factor of ×0.988 for reference-machine units, `reco-r3x`'s convention. The value it replaces came from `36b011f` and was the fast tail of its own distribution: every gate run since has read above it, which is a bias wearing a baseline, and the tail crossings read as `regression`s on a pane that had not moved. This row has measured 150.3-170.3 ms in every run since the bless against a bless of 138.3, and the ten probes sit at 150.6-154.7; the floor it is judged by stays the 25 ms spawn noise, so the row remains one the ±15 % ratchet cannot resolve and the 3 000 ms budget is what guards it

store.bytes_per_commit_graph.small.how: 258,048 `dbstat` bytes of `graph_*` over the 32 revisions the lane holds after one cold index (3 full snapshots, 560 delta rows). The denominator is a revision, as it is for `s3`'s 22 335 B and `e3.2`'s 6 041 B in §13.7 — not a commit of history: over the 500 commits in the fixture this is 516 B/commit, and that quotient falls as a repository ages, because the lane is a window and not a ledger (`reco-7yq`)

store.bytes_per_commit_spine.small.how: 733,184 spine bytes — `git_commit`, `git_commit_file`, `ref_tip` and their indexes — over 500 commits, `dbstat` pages of the store a cold index leaves; the same file holds 258,048 bytes of graph lane, 765,952 of cache and session rows and 1,781,760 of episodes, blobs and ledger, and none of them are charged here (`reco-7yq`)

warm.reindex.ms.small.how: one new commit with unique content, then `fathom index`. Re-blessed by `reco-axp`: the row was last blessed by `reco-r3x`, before `reco-dkr` moved the timed clock from the harness's 2 ms poll loop to the child's exit, and every wall clock in the file that predates that move carries a toll the measurement no longer contains — this one has measured 101.5-107.0 ms on this corpus since, 11-15 % under its bless, which tripped `stale_baseline` on alternate runs (a coin toss wearing a gate's badge, which is what `reco-axp` was filed about). Times are divided by this runner's calibration factor of ×0.988 so they stay in reference-machine units, the convention `reco-r3x` set, and the row now carries the centre and floor it was blessed with, as `reco-dkr` requires

warm.reindex.noop.ms.small.how: the run's own store-side `elapsed_ms` from `fathom index --json` — like §13.3's prototype rows, like the `warm.reindex.scaling_ratio` rationale, and like the `ctrl-r` this budget is written for, which re-indexes inside a process already running. The same 5 runs timed fork to exit are 15.9 ms, which is the toll every verb pays: process start, `Repository::discover`, `Store::open`

write.batch_rows/one_batch_at_the_cap.how: criterion: one batched transaction at the `write.batch_rows` cap

note: Rewritten only by `make bench-bless`. Every value is a measurement, in reference-machine units (runner factor 1.0); a time budget gets the factor as headroom at gate time and an RSS budget never does (ADR-004 §11.8).
